landing.subtitle: XIVIZLEY is a visual infrastructure tool for self-hosters and server administrators. Drag and connect containers, detect port conflicts instantly, and generate error-free docker-compose.yml in one click.
landing.howSubtitle: Build production-ready infrastructure in minutes with a developer-friendly 4-step workflow.
landing.step1Desc: Choose from 60+ curated self-hosted and cloud modules or define custom Docker containers with your own ports and volumes.
landing.step2Desc: Connect microservices visually and automatically build container dependency graphs (depends_on).
landing.step3Desc: Real-time port collision engine flags overlaps (e.g. Port 80, 53) and suggests smart available alternatives.
landing.step4Desc: Generate clean, standard docker-compose.yml and automated bash deploy scripts in a single click.
landing.privacyDesc: All Docker configurations and port calculations happen 100% inside your browser. Your designs are never shared with third parties unless you explicitly publish them to the community.
landing.ctaDesc: Free and no installation required. Start building in your browser right away.

about.title: About
about.subtitle: An open-source visual tool for designing your self-hosted and server architectures.

about.missionDesc: Bringing together the most powerful Docker and self-hosted applications in the open-source world so developers and system administrators can reduce infrastructure setup times to seconds.

privacy.title: Privacy & Data Security Policy
privacy.subtitle: At XIVIZLEY, we value transparency. We honestly explain how your data is handled.
privacy.card1Desc: The nodes, port configurations, and generated Docker Compose files you create on the XIVIZLEY canvas are processed entirely in your browser's local memory (client-side). Only when you use the 'Deploy to Server' (Cloud Push or one-line Run command) feature is your deployment template securely transmitted to your target server with token authentication; no environment variables or passwords are stored on our servers.
privacy.card2Desc: When you sign in with Google or GitHub OAuth providers, only the basic profile information required to verify your identity (name, email address, profile photo) is stored in our secure PostgreSQL database with encrypted session tokens. Your passwords are never stored on our servers.
privacy.card3Desc: When you publish your architecture using the Share to Community option, the title, description, and module list you choose are shared in the open community feed for other developers. We recommend checking your private passwords and sensitive environment variables before publishing.
privacy.card4Desc: XIVIZLEY does not sell data to advertising companies and does not host third-party advertising trackers that monitor user behavior.
privacy.card5Desc: The XIVIZLEY deployment script (deploy.sh) installs a lightweight monitoring CLI utility to /usr/local/bin/durum so you can easily view your active containers and resources via SSH. This tool runs 100% locally, sends no telemetry or data to external servers, and can be removed at any time.
privacy.footer: © XIVIZLEY Server Architect. Developed with an open-source vision.

guide.heroSubtitle: Step-by-step guide from visual canvas usage to VDS deployment, port management to AI Architect features.
guide.readyDesc: Start building your first architecture directly in your browser without any installation.
guide.footer: © XIVIZLEY Server Architect. Open-source community-driven infrastructure platform.
guide.s1p: XIVIZLEY is a visual Docker infrastructure design tool built for self-hosters, system administrators, and developers. Instead of wrestling with complex YAML files and port conflicts, you can drag and drop services onto a canvas, connect them, and export them error-free.
guide.s1f2desc: All calculations happen on your device.
guide.s1f3desc: Deploy to VDS with a single SSH command.
guide.s2p: There are two easy ways to add and configure services on the canvas:
guide.s2li1: Drag any service from the module library in the left menu (e.g. Nginx Proxy, Minecraft, Nextcloud) to any point on the canvas.
guide.s2li2: Click directly on the service card in the left panel to automatically add it to the center of the canvas.
guide.s2connectDesc: When you drag from the connection handle on the right side of a service to the handle on the left side of another, a dependency line is created. This connection is automatically handled as depends_on in Docker Compose.
guide.s3p: The most common problem in self-hosted setups is multiple services trying to use the same port. XIVIZLEY detects this instantly on the canvas:
guide.s3conflictDesc: If two services are assigned to the same host port, the card flashes red and the conflict count is shown in the top navbar. Click the "Configure" button on the card to change the port or select one of the suggested alternative ports.
guide.s4title: 4. Smart Stack Building with AI Architect
guide.s4p: If you don't know where to start or want to quickly set up a scenario, click the "Build with AI" button at the top of the left menu.
guide.s4ex1: "Automated media server with Plex, Radarr and Torrent"
guide.s4ex2: "Secure network infrastructure with AdGuard Home and WireGuard VPN"
guide.s4aiDesc: Our AI engine analyzes your request, selects the necessary services, arranges ports, and places them on the canvas within seconds.
guide.s5p: When you complete your architecture, click the "Deploy to Server" button in the upper right to open the deployment window.
guide.s5step1title: Connect to Your Server via SSH
guide.s5step2desc: Copy the curl ... | bash command from the deploy window and paste it into your terminal. The script performs pre-flight checks, installs Docker if not present, and brings up your entire stack.
guide.s6p: Keyboard shortcuts and export tools for faster work:
guide.s6exportDesc: Download your architecture visually with the PNG and SVG buttons at the bottom of the canvas, or generate a unique link to share with friends using the Share button.
guide.s7q1: Q: Are my server passwords or configurations saved on your server?
guide.s7a1: No. The XIVIZLEY architecture canvas runs 100% client-side. Your passwords and environment variables are not stored on our databases. During deployment, configuration files are transmitted solely with your confirmation via one-time encrypted token verification directly to your own server.
guide.s7q2: Q: Can I add my own custom Docker image?
guide.s7a2: Yes! Click the "+ Add Custom Container" button in the left menu to add any Docker image from Docker Hub or a private registry to the canvas.
guide.s7q3: Q: Can I manually download the generated docker-compose.yml file?
guide.s7a3: Absolutely. Download docker-compose.yml, deploy.sh, and README.md files in one click from the Output Panel on the right or from the "Deploy to Server > Download File Package" tab.
